correctness.rationale: The narrowed finding is exact synchronous stopping at d−1. Round r distinguishes each marker distance truncated at r+1. At round d−1 the distances are exact; a distance d forces s=d−t, otherwise the needed simultaneous-decrement neighbor pair is visible at round d−2 (the count is zero if a target distance is negative). Recovering s recovers the whole triple, and these are orbits of a color-preserving subgroup, so the partition is equitable. For the lower bound the pairs (d,d) and (d−1,d) are indistinguishable through d−2 by regular-graph locality but split in the next round. The complete-graph case d=1 starts equitable. A separate direct-graph replay corroborated the stopping round and orbit data in 24 nonbinary cases (up to 243 vertices) and reproduced the antipodal binary exception. The frozen finite outputs are recorded evidence, not a proof; the uploaded script was not executed.
